1.why: verify-token explicitly checks token.sessionId === session.id and token.accountBinding, so the reset code is bound to the requesting user/session.

2.why: Tokens are single-use (token.used = true) and bound to the originating sessionId, so the same code cannot work for any other user; the statement is false.

3.why: Setting a new password only flips session.passwordChanged; no session invalidation occurs, so any existing sessions remain valid until their 30-minute expiry.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and an HSTS header, so HTTPS is enforced, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as bcrypt hashes (appropriate cryptographic protection), though this is hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: No email is ever sent; the mock delivery prints the recovery token and link to the browser console and Logs panel, so no guarded email message exists.

7.why: Inputs are validated (type/length checks, strict token regex, body-size cap) and output is written via textContent into fixed markup, though contact input is only length-validated rather than deeply sanitized.

8.why: Only same-origin relative links are used, view navigation is restricted to an allowlist, and there is no redirect mechanism to external sites.

9.why: No email templates exist; the single page is fixed markup with nonce-protected scripts/styles and no user input interpolated into HTML.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the client-side Logs panel and console deliberately display the recovery token and MFA code, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and reset tokens stored as hashes, but the MFA secret code "482913" is hardcoded in the source and returned to the client.

12.why: No default username/password exists (passwordHash starts empty and there is no login endpoint), but the hardcoded MFA code functions as a fixed, known credential for that step.

13.why: Per-category failure counters lock the session for 5 minutes after 5 failures and return 429 responses for recovery, token, MFA, and password attempts.

14.why: recovery-request always returns the identical generic message "If an eligible account exists, recovery instructions have been sent." regardless of input validity.

15.why: The reset code is a 256-bit CSPRNG value, stored hashed, single-use, 10-minute TTL, and bound to both the sessionId and the account binding.
